rfm_tuples.R: 'Same-Shack sales 1 for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 increased 2.3% compared to the same period last year, driven by a 3.1% increase in price mix, partially offset by a 0.8% decline in guest traffic. ... Same-Shack sales 1 for the fiscal fourth quarter ended December 31, 2025 increased 2.1% ... driven by a 1.6% increase in price mix and a 0.5% increase in guest traffic.' CEO 4Q25 letter cites '20 consecutive quarters of positive same-Shack sales growth.'
rfm_tuples.f: If the SSS narrative were durable, subsequent 8-K/10-Q disclosures should reaffirm the SSS metric and the price-led / improving-traffic framing. A subsequent silent-disappearance or downward revision would be concerning.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 15 subsequent mentions across 8-K filings (window 2025-02-22 → 2026-05-20). Classification AFFIRMED in 4Q25 shareholder letter, which explicitly quantifies +2.1% Q4 / +2.3% FY and asserts '20 consecutive quarters of positive same-Shack sales growth.' Evolution status = REAFFIRMED_IN_8K_ONLY.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: SSS metric is reaffirmed across cadence — not a fabrication. BUT the composition is weak: full-year SSS is entirely price-driven (+3.1% price vs -0.8% traffic). Average weekly sales fell from $79K to $77K in Q4 and were flat for the year. Restaurant-level economics are decaying on a per-Shack basis even as price-led SSS prints positive. The +2.3% FY number is also augmented by a 53rd operating week in fiscal 2025 not present in 2024 — a calendar tailwind the company discloses but does not fully wash out of the headline.

rfm_tuples.R: Restaurant-level profit margin '22.6%' for FY25 vs 21.4% FY24 vs 19.9% FY23. Adjusted EBITDA margin 14.5% / 14.0% / 12.1%. Net income $49.7M / $10.8M / $21.0M; Income from operations $62.5M / $3.0M / $5.9M. Implied claim: margin expansion is real and structural.
rfm_tuples.f: If margin recovery is structural (not just price-led under-investment), restaurant-level margin should hold in a year with rising labor cost regimes (NY/CA limited-service wages). BLS QCEW NY County NAICS-7225 wage cost trajectory is the most direct benchmark.
rfm_tuples.M_value: NY County limited-service restaurants (NAICS 7225) Q4 2024: 8,265 establishments, 155,433 average employees, average weekly wage $965 — confirming the high-cost labor market that drove the FY20-23 margin compression. SHAK's 22.6% restaurant-level margin is improving on the prior 2 years AND occurs alongside a 53-week fiscal year (one extra operating week of fixed-cost leverage), and includes a $5.2M impairment & closure charge vs $32.4M in 2024 — i.e. margin is partially flattered by absence of prior-year impairment.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Margin trajectory is genuinely improving, but the headline +120 bps Restaurant-level / +50 bps Adj EBITDA YoY needs two haircuts: (a) 53rd week adds ~1.9% to revenue with disproportionate fixed-cost leverage (margin boost), and (b) FY24 impairments were $32M vs $5M FY25, a $27M YoY headwind reversal. Net of both, like-for-like restaurant-level margin expansion is closer to 50-70 bps, not 120 bps. Real improvement but the 10-K framing modestly oversells it.

rfm_tuples.R: 'opening of 45 new Company-operated Shacks in fiscal 2025'; CEO 4Q25 letter calls it 'our largest class yet' and reiterates 'long-term targets.' Total system 659 Shacks (373 Company / 286 licensed). 2025 capex increased $30.3M YoY driven by larger development pipeline.
rfm_tuples.f: If unit-growth cadence is being executed as claimed, the 10-K's per-state property table should reconcile to the 373 Company-operated count, and AUV/AWS should not be collapsing (which would indicate cannibalization or weakened new-Shack economics).
rfm_tuples.M_source: Filing cross-read (Item 2 Properties geographic table; MD&A Key Operating Metrics)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Properties table sums to exactly 373 Company-operated domestic + 47 licensed domestic + 239 licensed international = 659 system-wide, matching the headline. New U.S. concentration: TX (27), CA (50), NY (55 Company / 12 lic), FL (25). Average Weekly Sales declined from $79K to $77K Q4 YoY and was flat for FY at $76K — confirming new-Shack openings are NOT lifting AUV. Cash $360M is well above the $30M incremental capex.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Unit count reconciles cleanly (no opening-pace fabrication). HOWEVER the company's 'largest class yet' framing obscures that AWS is FLAT-to-DOWN as new units open — classic unit-economic dilution. With AWS declining in Q4 and Restaurant-level margin only marginally expanding once the 53-week and impairment haircut is applied, the implied long-term unit-growth math (which assumes new-Shack AUV near maturity) is materially weaker than the narrative. This is a moderate forward-fundamentals concern, not a balance-sheet risk.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We believe our existing cash and cash equivalents balances and cash from operations will be sufficient to fund our operating and finance lease obligations, capital expenditures, Tax Receivable Agreement obligations and working capital needs for at least the next 12 months. ... As of December 31, 2025, we were in compliance with all covenants.' $360.1M cash, no revolver drawn, $250M 0% Convertible Notes due Mar 2028.
rfm_tuples.f: If liquidity is genuinely strong, going-concern detector should be NEGATIVE and no auditor turnover should have occurred.
rfm_tuples.M_value: going_concern: 0 matches in 10-K, signal=NO_GOING_CONCERN. auditor: 0 Item 4.01 8-Ks in 5-year lookback, signal=CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE. Cash $360M > Convertible Notes face $250M; operating cash flow $222.4M FY25.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Liquidity narrative is verified. SHAK is genuinely cash-rich relative to its only material maturity (the $250M 0% Convert due March 2028). Operating cash flow alone could repay the convert. Clean auditor tenure across 5-year lookback supports management-narrative reliability. This is NOT a balance-sheet distress story — the -56% drawdown is a growth-narrative / multiple-compression story, not solvency.

rfm_tuples.R: Sixth Amendment to Revolving Credit Facility (July 9, 2025) extends maturity to earlier of Feb 28, 2028 or 91 days prior to Convertible Notes maturity. Notable precursor: 'Fifth Amendment AND Waiver' (March 19, 2025) — the explicit waiver language indicates a covenant breach or technical condition was waived. Revolver requires compliance with maximum net lease adjusted leverage + minimum fixed charge coverage ratios.
rfm_tuples.f: If 5th Amendment & Waiver were materially adverse (covenant breach), we would expect either follow-on borrowings under distress or accelerated UCC-1 / secured-debt activity, plus possibly auditor turnover.
rfm_tuples.M_value: UCC proxy: 12 secured-debt term hits across 10-K/10-Qs over 36 mo window, 5 distress terms ('all assets' x5, 'lien' x3, 'pledged collateral' x2, 'first-priority lien' x2), 0 Item 2.03 8-Ks, no 6-mo cluster, signal=ELEVATED_LIEN_EXPOSURE. Auditor tenure CLEAN. Revolver remains undrawn at year-end 2025 ($0 outstanding); 10-K affirms 'in compliance with all covenants.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Fifth Amendment AND Waiver in March 2025 (cited in the exhibit index but not narratively explained in the MD&A excerpt) is the single most telling under-discussed item in the filing. A 'waiver' under a Revolving Credit Facility almost always signals a covenant condition requiring lender forbearance. The Sixth Amendment 4 months later then re-papered the maturity. Even though year-end status is 'in compliance' and revolver is undrawn, the existence of the waiver indicates the covenant cushion at some point in H1 2025 was thin enough to require lender consent — likely tied to the net lease adjusted leverage ratio as restaurant-level losses absorbed the operating-lease ramp. This is the kind of small-print signal that the deep-trough drawdown is partially pricing.

rfm_tuples.R: International presence claim: 239 licensed international Shacks across 19 countries (51 in Mainland China/HK/Macau, 34 South Korea, 21 Mexico, 18 Japan, 17 England, 15 UAE, 14 Kuwait, 12 Turkey). System-wide sales +15.9% to $2,228.8M FY25; licensing revenue $54.1M FY25 vs $45.0M FY24 (+20.2%).
rfm_tuples.f: If international licensee network is real and growing, licensing revenue should scale with disclosed unit count, and there should be no concentration disaster (e.g., one bankrupt licensee collapsing a region).
rfm_tuples.M_source: Filing cross-read (Item 2 Properties + MD&A Licensing Revenue)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Licensing revenue $54.1M / 239 international + 47 domestic licensed = 286 licensed units → ~$189K licensing revenue per licensed unit; using system-wide sales attributable to licensed (~$837M implied from $2,228.8M system - $1,391M Company-operated Shack sales), licensing royalty implied rate ~6.5% of licensed system sales, consistent with industry norm 5-8% for premium QSR franchising. No bankrupt-licensee disclosure. Geographic concentration: Greater China (51 = 21% of intl units) is highest single bucket; not extreme.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: International licensing narrative is internally consistent and economically plausible. Royalty math reconciles. No outsized single-country concentration that would create a cliff. The +20.2% licensing revenue growth meaningfully outpaces the +14.7% U.S. Shack-sales growth, validating that the licensed/international leg is the cleaner growth engine. PASS.

rfm_tuples.interpretation: Legal-proceeding narrative is verified. Insider sales are tiny ($12M aggregate over 12 months for a ~$3-4B market cap), entirely 10b5-1, no clustering. The 2023 restatement is now mature (referenced in Adj EBITDA add-backs as 'Restatement costs' $354K FY24 trailing to $0 in FY25), so it is not a live forward exposure. PASS.

rfm_tuples.R: Implicit counterparty claim: Shake Shack's digital sales narrative depends heavily on third-party delivery aggregators (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub) — the 'digital and delivery strategy' is listed as a top risk factor. The 10-K does not name or quantify aggregator concentration but the relationships are operationally material to the SSS/traffic mix.
rfm_tuples.f: If the aggregator partnerships are material to either party, megacap-side filings (Uber, DoorDash) might mention Shake Shack as a noteworthy partner OR — alternatively — restaurant brands are typically too granular to be named individually in delivery-platform 10-Ks.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 0 hits across Uber and DoorDash 10-K/10-Q/8-K filings over 10-year window mentioning 'Shake Shack'. Signal=INFLATION_SUSPECT.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The INFLATION_SUSPECT signal is a known false-positive in restaurant verticals: delivery aggregators have thousands of restaurant partners and disclose at the segment/category level (restaurant GMV, take rate), never naming individual chain partners in SEC filings even when material to the restaurant counterparty. Absence here is therefore NOT informative — UNVERIFIABLE, drop from composite. The risk-factor language about digital/delivery concentration is real but cannot be adjudicated via megacap-side disclosure.

summary: SHAK is a genuinely cash-rich ($360M cash, no revolver drawn, clean auditor, NO_GOING_CONCERN) growth-restaurant whose -56% trough is NOT a fraud or solvency story but rather (a) decelerating unit economics (AWS flat-to-down, traffic -0.8% FY, margin gains partially flattered by 53rd-week + reversed FY24 impairment), (b) an under-discussed Fifth Amendment AND Waiver to the revolver in March 2025 signaling H1 2025 covenant pressure that the MD&A doesn't narratively explain, and (c) larger 2025 capex pipeline against a softening per-unit revenue trend. International licensing is the cleaner growth leg. Composite 0.571 across 7 verifiable claims (3 PASS / 4 MODERATE / 0 SEVERE / 0 RED FLAG; 1 UNVERIFIABLE).
